Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

None of today's forms record stop-work authority being exercised. Across every air job submitted on 11/05, the item selected was "Stop work authority was discussed" — the routine pre-job item — and "Stop work authority utilized" was selected on no form at all. The items below are selections that need the technician's confirmation of what was meant, consistent with Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance that this is a training matter rather than a set of events.
"Unsafe conditions" selected with no narrative describing one — four forms:
1099 William Jimmy Cooper — XTO Turner 1201 #6, job 36491, 1:59 PM. Narrative fields read "Team work", "Work together", "Same as we found it".
1099 William Jimmy Cooper — XTO Turner 1201 #2, job 36493, 12:34 PM. Narrative reads "Adherence to safety rules"; "Details if Any" is blank.
1099 William Jimmy Cooper — XTO Turner 1201 #21, job 36489, 11:22 AM, first of three OWL submissions. Narrative reads "Good safety habits".

Michael Jobe — XTO Baumann 16 #1, job 36589, 11:53 AM. Narrative reads "Everyone stayed out the way when killing the well", which describes personnel keeping clear during a well kill rather than naming a condition.

Worth separating out: Cooper selected "Unsafe conditions" on all three of his Turner 1201 jobs, and the selected strings on those forms are near-identical to one another. That pattern points to a selection being carried forward between jobs rather than made fresh each time, which is the training point rather than three separate events. Michael Jobe's form is the one that sits differently: he selected "Unsafe conditions" while selecting neither stop-work item, on a well-kill job. Worth asking him directly what he was marking.

Repeat from previous days: Michael Jobe appeared on this list twice in one day on 09/26 for the same pattern — "Unsafe conditions" selected with no supporting narrative — and appears on it again today. Nathan Contreras, who was on the stop-work confirmation list on 09/23 and again on 09/26, selected neither stop-work item today and is not on this list.

The inverse check: no air job narrative on 11/05 describes a real unsafe condition while leaving "Unsafe conditions" unselected. The genuine equipment findings today came through the trailer forms instead, and are listed above.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. In particular, fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates, SCBA and workpack inspection sheet contents, mask bag sticker dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images and not as text fields, so this review can confirm that a photo was taken and when, but not what it shows. The one exception today is where a technician typed the problem into a note, which is how three of the five safety concerns above were found.

66 of 66 submissions read. Both job boards were available: the 11/05/2026 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin boards from Blake Walton's email of 11/05 at 10:12 AM Central, using the "11-5" sheet of each. 52 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 40 on the Permian Basin board and 12 on the ArkLaTex board — after excluding contingency, shop, WTX-support and days-off rows. This review ran at approximately 10:05 PM Central on 11/05, so any submission filed after that hour, and any form for 11/05 that arrives tomorrow morning, is not included.
